metadata.title: High-Performance Computing Core

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for operating shared high-performance computing platforms in a manner that preserves isolation, integrity, and availability across diverse workloads.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: High-performance computing clusters, batch schedulers, shared accelerators, and tightly coupled compute fabrics.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Pattern for establishing baseline trust assumptions for shared and scheduler-mediated high-performance computing environments.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: HPC trust assumptions depend on the physical and operational hosting environment.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: HPC platforms commonly rely on trusted bare-metal execution substrates.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Privilege escalation risks arising from scheduler abuse or shared compute context.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Lateral movement between jobs or users executing on shared compute nodes.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Impact to availability or integrity of shared compute resources.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Privilege escalation through exploitation of shared operating system or scheduler context.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Denial-of-service through exhaustion or monopolization of shared compute resources.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Execution isolation between workloads running on shared compute nodes.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Privileged access management for scheduler and platform administration.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Reduction of attack surface exposed by shared HPC platform services.

metadata.remarks: High-Performance Computing Core defines the foundational trust properties required to operate shared, performance-oriented compute platforms. This pattern recognizes that HPC environments emphasize throughput and flexibility, and therefore makes scheduler-mediated execution, shared-resource risk, and platform-level isolation explicit.

components.title: Shared Node Isolation
components.description: Prevents interference between concurrent workloads executing on shared compute nodes.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Isolation mechanisms prevent one workload from impacting the execution of others on shared nodes.

components.title: Scheduler-Mediated Execution Trust
components.description: Establishes trust boundaries enforced by batch and job schedulers.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Schedulers enforce workload separation, resource allocation, and execution constraints.

components.title: Compute Resource Fairness
components.description: Limits abusive or monopolizing use of shared compute resources.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Resource controls prevent single workloads or users from denying service to others.
